reader.requirement: At --std 85, for an indexed file that contains variable length records (RECORD IS VARYING, or a Format 3 RECORD CONTAINS i4 TO i5 / no RECORD clause where the implementor chooses variable records, II.2.1.4.3, VII.3.8.4 GR13), the compiler must refuse a RECORD KEY whose character positions reach past x = the file's minimum record size (integer-2 when stated, else the least size described for a record, VII.3.8.4 GR4/GR6, with an ODO table at its minimum, GR5a), and accept a key ending at or before x; a fixed-length file is outside the rule.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel < 2002 selects Rules85 = the 2023 rows minus those a 1985 row Supersedes, plus Rules1985 (SR2 category/location and SR3 group-with-ODO rows). The SR4 row SR-12.4.5.12.3-4 is superseded by no 1985 row, so the same row runs at 85 and 2023

VaryingRecordInfo.BoundsEnforced for Format 3 (RECORD CONTAINS i4 TO i5) via DialectBehavior.RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize (active from 2002): at 85 the Format 3 integers are not the minimum, so FileModel.VaryMin falls to the smallest record description (VII.3.8.4 GR14: i4 'refer[s] to the minimum number of characters in the smallest size data record'); at 2023 integer-4 is the minimum

reader.edition-search: Read FileControlKeyRules.Rules/Rules1985/RulesFor/Screen/BeyondMinimum and FileModel.VaryMin/VaryMax/RecordSizeVaries/ImpliesVariableFormat; grep 'BoundsEnforced' and 'RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize' to find the record-clause edition arm.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: for a Format 3 RECORD CONTAINS i4 TO i5 clause the minimum is the smallest record description at 85 and integer-4 from 2002; for VARYING FROM integer-2 and for no clause the minimum is the same at both
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1025 covers RECORD IS VARYING FROM 10 TO 50 only; Format 3, VARYING without FROM, multi-record and ODO-record files and the exact boundary are covered by probes

reader.notes: The 2023 SR4 row runs unchanged at 85 because 1985's rule is the same test; the minimum it measures against is FileModel.VaryMin, whose only edition arm is the Format 3 integers (correctly not the minimum at 85, per GR14). Files with no RECORD clause are fixed under the implementation's documented choice, so the rule rightly does not fire on m1/o1/o3. The diagnostic cites §2023:12.4.5.12.3 SR4 at --std 85 (presentation only).

refuter.evidence: cite.py: OK §1985:IX.2.7.3 SR4; OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR5a ('The minimum number of table elements described in the record is used'); OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR6. Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-05/c3, aimed at the minimum the reader did not exercise: k2 VARYING (no FROM), a short record 4 + ODO 0 TO 6 (min 4, max 10) and the key in another record at bytes 5..9 -> COBOL0863 'minimum size 4' (the ODO is measured at its minimum, not its maximum); k7 same with ODO 1 TO 6 (min 5) and a 1-byte key at byte 5 -> OPEN=00 (exact boundary accepted); k3 VARYING FROM 4 and k5 Format 3 'RECORD CONTAINS 4 TO 20' with the same records -> COBOL0863 minimum 4; k4 key in the fixed part before an ODO -> OPEN=00; k1 a SYNCHRONIZED binary item in the short record -> minimum 5, consistent with the documented no-slack layout (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-197: no implicit FILLER for SYNCHRONIZED, so GR5's 'plus any implicit FILLER' adds nothing); k6 a 2002 'RECORD KEY IS RK SOURCE IS A' -> COBOL0900 requires COBOL-2002. No hole found.
